title: What If Every Frog Vanished?

scenes.text: What if every frog vanished? Central America got a preview, and malaria rose.
From the early 1980s a fungus swept through Costa Rica and Panama, wiping out amphibians. Worldwide it has hit over five hundred species.
In 1980 both countries had fewer than a thousand malaria cases. Frogs eat mosquitoes, and with fewer of them the bugs may have thrived.
Cases rose right after the die-offs began and peaked five to six years later.
Costa Rica hit about seven thousand cases in the mid-1990s. Panama reached about five thousand in the mid-2000s.
Researchers say more work is needed to prove the link. But small animals can hold up big systems.

What if every frog vanished?
When a fungus wiped out amphibians in Costa Rica and Panama, malaria cases rose right after, peaking five to six years later, according to a UC Davis-led study.
